response: Yes, increases in the cigarette tax rate can be linked to cigarette retail prices. When the tax rate on cigarettes increases, manufacturers and retailers typically pass the additional cost on to consumers by raising the retail price of cigarettes. This is because the tax is usually added to the wholesale or retail price of the cigarettes, so retailers increase their prices to maintain their profit margins. As a result, higher cigarette tax rates are often associated with higher retail prices for cigarettes.
